rationale: bugs_open/331 (filed from the bugs_open/286 close, 2026-08-19). create_tool_component — the tool-generator's save_tool action, the single live step naming it — has a CREATE path and no REPLACE path. The write history is the evidence: agent_error_log holds exactly ONE duplicate-key row per gate on three consecutive days — 08-15 pages_site_id_name_key (bugs_closed/286, fixed+live), 08-17 idx_cc_tool_function_unique (RFC_036 §9.3, e24bc9c0f, APPROVED ceae30f2, LIVE on v1.0.1316), 08-18 content_components_name_key (UNIQUE(name), no predicate; name = function+'-'+domainSlug; NO handler in any Go writer). Plus the silent gate: the per-site already_exists probe returns {already_exists:true} and writes nothing; nothing reads that key, and enqueue_rerender then lacks create_result.page_id, so a re-fix run reports complete having changed nothing. The webdesign_tool_rebuilds lane (12 tools replaced, 51 to go, owner ruling 2026-08-19 'framework ownership of all 63, fixes must extend into the framework') works round all of this by hand on every re-fix: UPDATE content_components SET is_active=false, rename the old row, build, then UPDATE page_components SET build_status='removed' on the old slot BEFORE the generator's own rerender is claimed — a race measured at 2–96 minutes with no floor, lost once (the page served BOTH tools). Their words: 'the generator can build a given tool for a given site EXACTLY ONCE, EVER … the recipe could ship a tool but never fix one.' THE CHANGE: a per-ITEM optional input `replace_existing` (ActionInputSpec.Optional 3→4, RFC_022 N=10; mapped STRICTLY by seed 496 as "replace_existing!": "input_data.spec.replace_existing" so the RFC_029 whole-tree search can never supply it). Absent ⇒ byte-identical today — the probe's short-circuit stays because it IS the per-site throttle that keeps a duplicate add_tool (the suggester re-suggesting a tool the site has) a no-op; a STEP flag would turn every duplicate into a live regeneration, which is why authority is per item (LANDMINES 'why not just fix the query' is right and this keeps it right). Set + incumbent found ⇒ REGENERATE IN PLACE: the section writer's own convention (CTS-009; store_generated_component's regeneration branch; lookupBaseComponent omits is_active precisely because the alternative is the name collision above — the estate already learned this once). Snapshot the incumbent template to component_versions via the section writer's snapshotComponentVersion (reused, not copied), ask the shared-template fence sharedComponentWriteCheck (bugs_open/285; refuse an incumbent placed on >1 site, or an unreadable census — a new arm has no legacy to fail towards), then in ONE transaction: lock the incumbent's live agent-writable placements on this site (FOR UPDATE; build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'; pageComponentAgentWritableSQL honoured — a human-locked slot refuses), UPDATE the incumbent row's html_template/display_name/description/category/provenance, UPDATE those placements' rendered_html + build_status='deployed'. Tools carry the template verbatim as rendered_html (what this action's own link INSERT and deploy_tool write; the assembler reads rendered_html and never re-renders a slot from the template, so a 'pending' flip alone would leave the OLD tool serving) — and that rendered_html UPDATE fires trg_page_component_artefact_archive_upd, so page_component_history keeps the old bytes: the revert handle a status flip never produced and the lane had to record md5s for by hand. forked_from/name/function untouched ⇒ zero uniqueness gates; RFC_036 §9.3's lookup cannot record the replacement as a fork of the row it replaces (the wrinkle any second-row design has: retire v1 and the function leaves the library); the page never holds two tool slots, so the retire race is gone. Result carries regenerated:true, the SAME component_id, page_id/page_url/function (what compose_plan/write_plan/index_plan/enqueue_rerender read; write_doc_plan supersedes by subject so a regeneration correctly replaces the travelling plan), page_adopted:true (the lane's grading key), slots_updated, previous_version. The creation-only tail (nav rebuild, content item, cross-links, guide) is skipped — those exist from the first build; a regeneration is a content change, which is what lets it be one transaction. Flag set with NO incumbent ⇒ today's greenfield walk, pinned. GUARDS: the two source-scan coverage tests caught the new writer — component_template_writer_coverage_test is satisfied by CALLING the fence; page_component_writer_coverage_test gets a declared EXEMPTION with reason (a per-item rebuild is SUPPOSED to change the markup — the component_swap judgement in single_slot_floors.go's own scope table, whose 'create_tool_component: INSERT only' row is corrected in the same change). Residual stated: a hollow regeneration (zero visible text) passes every gate; a text-content floor is owed elsewhere (286's related finding). Tests: 5 sqlmock arms, two mutation-proven (deleting the slot UPDATE breaks the walk at COMMIT; deleting the zero-placement guard turns the typed refusal into an unexpected UPDATE); full actions package green on archive-HEAD; cmd/config-key-audit parity green after check.py OPTIONAL_KEY_COUNTS create_tool_component 3→4. CONSUMERS (RFC_022 enumeration, live DB 2026-08-19 16:03Z): exactly ONE step names create_tool_component — tool-generator.save_tool. Not architecture-scope by the 2026-08-11 ruling (opt-in, unsafe default OFF, one consumer). Convention recorded in RFC_036 §12 as the tool writer's third collision convention, keyed on who owns the incumbent (library claim → fork §9.3; own row → regenerate in place; sections divert CLC-020). The 090 diagnosis run (44ada235) is in flight; the bug file carries it. Commit will carry Council-Submitted; the lane's RUNBOOK hand steps are marked retired-for-re-fixes pending roll + seed.

-- 496_tool_generator_replace_existing_HOLD.sql
--
-- ⚠ HOLD until the chassis roll that carries create_tool_component's
-- replace_existing arm (bugs_open/331, register TL-047) has ROLLED. The `_HOLD`
-- suffix keeps the migration runner's --apply from taking it (SIDECAR_RE
-- excludes it; MEMORY "migration-runner-practice"). Image before config.
--
-- Safe-to-apply-early? Technically yes — the key is an INPUT MAPPING, not a
-- config switch: on the old binary `replace_existing` is not in the action's
-- ActionInputSpec, so the mapped value is simply unread (create_tool_component
-- has no ConfigKeys declaration, so there is no strict-config refusal either).
-- But applying it early invites a lane to file a `replace_existing: true` item
-- against the old binary, which would then take the already_exists short-circuit
-- and burn a generator round having changed nothing. So: HOLD anyway.
--
-- To apply after the roll: verify the binary carries the fix commit
--   (probe the STAMP, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix commit> <stamp>`,
--   with a junk-hex control — never "is my sha in the binary"),
-- then rename to 496_tool_generator_replace_existing.sql (drop _HOLD, fix the
-- two filename literals below) and apply.

--   "replace_existing!": "input_data.spec.replace_existing"
